review_notes: Read the whole file and the relevant parts of Opposite.lean (ExactStructure.op and its conflation lemmas). Opposite.lean imports only ExactStructure and Mathlib. No file in the repo has both Opposite and BaseChange upstream of the other, so adding `public import TauCeti.CategoryTheory.Exact.Opposite` to BaseChange.lean creates no cycle. I did not compile any rewrite. The op-transport steps below depend on the exact forms of `IsPullback.op`/`IsPushout.op` and on how `ShortComplex.op` unfolds, and I checked those only by hand. The two candidates were the only duplications I found. Beyond them, the Noether theorems `exists_conflation_comp` and `exists_conflation_comp'` are thin assemblies of the lemmas above. The `cobaseChange` and `baseChange` API blocks are short parallel definitions and simp lemmas, which fall below the rubric's threshold.

claims.reason: The two proofs are line-for-line duals: kernel-cokernel pair, E2 stability, Epi/Mono cancellation through v or ι, a `key` factorisation via `hpair.desc`/`hpair.lift` closed by `sq.hom_ext`, then `ofπ'`/`ofι'` with `.choose`. The reasoning is nontrivial and about 20 lines are written twice. Opposite.lean already supplies `ExactStructure.op` and `op_conflation_op_iff`, with the needed instances on Cᵒᵖ. It imports only ExactStructure, so there is no dependency cycle. For `S : ShortComplex C`, `S.op` runs `S.X₃ᵒᵖ ⟶ S.X₂ᵒᵖ ⟶ S.X₁ᵒᵖ`. The square `sq.op.flip : IsPushout S.op.f u.op v.op w.op` is a pushout of `S.op.f = S.g.op` along `u.op`. `cobaseChangeπ S.op sq.op.flip` is then the desc of `S.f.op` and `0`, which is `(baseChangeι S sq).op`. So `(baseChange S sq).op = cobaseChange S.op sq.op.flip` as short complexes, and the transport works. The benefit is moderate, since an identification lemma must be added, but it removes one of two parallel scripts.

theorem conflation_baseChange {S} (hS : E.Conflation S) {Z' Q} {u v w} (sq : IsPullback v w S.g u) : E.Conflation (baseChange S sq) := by
  rw [← E.op_conflation_op_iff, baseChange_op S sq]
  exact E.op.conflation_cobaseChange ((E.op_conflation_op_iff S).2 hS) sq.op.flip

claims.reason: `conflation_comp_of_isPullback` is the exact dual of `conflation_comp_of_isPushout`, and the two proofs repeat the same argument in the same order: kernel-cokernel pair, `isInflation_comp`/`isDeflation_comp`, Epi/Mono via `sq.hom_ext` plus cancel, a `key` factorisation, and `.choose`. Dualising by hand checks out. In `E.op`, take the first conflation `mk p.op i.op` and the second `mk q.op v.op`, with `sq.op.flip : IsPushout q.op i.op c.op α.op`. The pushout lemma then yields `E.op.Conflation (mk (p.op ≫ q.op) c.op _)`. That is `(mk c (q ≫ p) _).op` up to `op_comp`, so `op_conflation_op_iff` transports it back. The hypotheses match and there is no cycle. The edit needs a small `ShortComplex.op` rewrite, but it removes a full duplicate proof. The same transport could also derive `exists_conflation_comp'`, but that is optional.
claims.shared_lemma: Keep `conflation_comp_of_isPushout` as the single core proof. It is used in `E.op` with the opposite of the pullback data: `(ShortComplex.mk c (q ≫ p) _).op = ShortComplex.mk (p.op ≫ q.op) c.op _` (by `op_comp`/rfl-level rewriting), and `sq.op.flip : IsPushout q.op i.op c.op α.op`.

  have h₁' : E.op.Conflation (ShortComplex.mk p.op i.op _) := (E.op_conflation_op_iff (ShortComplex.mk i p hip)).2 h₁
